chapter: Postwar Chicago, Janis and De Paris
title: Rudi Blesh and Moore's first vocals
summary: Blesh chose him to sing because of his preacher-like voice and was easy to work for.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Whose idea was it for you to sing? Was it yours or was it Rudi Blesh, Conrad Janis...?
I see. Why did he select you?

Well, he knew I had that type of voice for numbers like that, you know. See, I've got one of them preacher things, like a preacher or a sanctified brother. [SINGS] "I'm gonna lay down my bur-den/Down by the river-side, down by the river-side..."
So he was impressed with that.
There we go. How was Rudi to work with in the recording studio? Was he a taskmaster? Did he like the music to be performed in a certain way? Or was he easy to please.
He was a very easy man to get along with. He knew what he wanted, and he'd continue until he finished that record out.
